sample_steps.rule: Start from the GEM Adult Population Survey harmonized individual file; keep respondents from the 24 countries named in the article: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States (COUNTRY / CTRYALP).
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.10 text; countries chosen as World Bank high-income and UNDP high human development

sample_steps.rule: Keep survey years GEM_YR 2001 through 2008. The article's realized set of country-year surveys is listed in the supplement; the article does not state a rule for why some fielded country-years are absent (see unavailable_or_unclear).
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.10 text; S1 p.1 Table A1 'Survey years' column

sample_steps.rule: Keep respondents in the labour force. Origin reading: currently working full- or part-time (GEMWORK codes 1 or 2; equivalently GEMWORK3 = 10). Footnote 2 and the supplement's 'not employed' control indicate that not-employed respondents are excluded from the main sample.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.10 text and fn 2; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 2 note

sample_steps.rule: Keep respondents 'over 18 and under 55 years old'. Origin reading: GEMAGE from 18 through 54 inclusive (GEM samples adults 18 and older). Alternative reading 19-54 recorded in spec_space.

Drop respondents with missing or non-substantive codes on gender (GEMSEX = 9), age (GEMAGE 99/999), education (GEMEDUC = 9999), work status (GEMWORK = 9) or the screening items used in the outcome (codes 8, 9). Listwise deletion is the implied rule; the article does not state it.
sample_steps.source_locator: unstated; implied by MAIN p.11 variable definitions

sample_steps.rule: Stage 1 analytic sample (Table 1 models and per-country logits): all respondents remaining after steps 1-5.

Stage 2 analytic sample (Table 2): restrict to established business owners, i.e. respondents who report currently owning and helping to manage a business (OWNMGE = 1) with the owner-manager module answered; drop cases missing on motivation (OMREASON), employees (OMNOWJOB), five-year jobs (OMYR5JOB), ownership share (OMOWN) or first-payment year (OMWAGEYR). Whether the GEM 42-month 'established' transform (OMESTBBT) was used instead is unclear.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.11 text and fn 3; MAIN p.14-15 variable definitions; S1 p.2 Table A2 Panel B heading

sample_steps.rule: Model 7 (new product/service): further restrict to survey years 2002-2008 because the item (OMNEWCST) was not asked in 2001.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.15 fn 14; MAIN p.22 Table 2 note †

sample_steps.rule: Model 8 (new technology): further restrict to survey years 2005-2008 because the item (OMNEWT_5) starts in 2005; this removes Poland, whose surveys predate 2005.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.15 fn 14; MAIN p.22 Table 2 note ‡

sample_steps.rule: Supplement Model 2 (full sample): apply steps 1, 2, 4, 5 but not step 3; add a 'not employed' indicator.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.10 fn 2; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 2 and note †

sample_steps.rule: Supplement Model 3 (perceptions): stage 1 sample further restricted to respondents with observed SUSKILL, FEARFAIL and KNOWENT; from 2003 these items were asked of all entrepreneurs but only a random half of non-entrepreneurs.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.11 text and fn 5; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 3

sample_steps.rule: Merge survey-level (country-year) variables to individuals by country and survey year; then standardize every survey-level variable (z-score) across the analytic survey-years.
sample_steps.source_locator: MAIN p.11 'Work-family institutions variables'; MAIN p.14 'All survey-level variables are standardized'

variables.name: entrepreneurial_activity
variables.definition: 1 if the respondent is a nascent entrepreneur (actively trying to start a business, alone or with others, and has not paid salaries, wages or payments in kind for more than three months) or an established business owner (currently owner of a business she or he helps manage); 0 otherwise.
variables.construction: Origin: BSTART = 1 and not (SUWAGE = 1 with payments for more than three months) [i.e. nascent per fn 3], OR OWNMGE = 1. Alternative using GEM transforms: SUBOANWT = 1 or OMBABYBT = 1 or OMESTBBT = 1 (see spec_space).
variables.coding_of_missing: Codes 8 (don't know) and 9 (refused/missing) on BSTART/OWNMGE treated as missing (unstated; pre-2002 GEM practice treated don't know as no).
variables.locator: MAIN p.11 text and fn 3; S1 p.2 Table A2 Panel A row 'Entrepreneur'

variables.name: nascent_entrepreneur
variables.definition: 1 if actively trying to start a business and has not paid wages for more than three months; 0 otherwise (supplement Model 1).
variables.construction: BSTART = 1 and not yet paying wages more than three months (SUWAGE); or GEM transform SUBOANWT = 1.
variables.locator: MAIN p.11 fn 3; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 1

variables.name: female
variables.definition: 1 = female, 0 = male
variables.construction: GEMSEX = 2 -> 1; GEMSEX = 1 -> 0

variables.name: age
variables.definition: age in years, grand-mean centered
variables.construction: GEMAGE minus the analytic-sample mean
variables.transformations: grand-mean centering (fn 4); squared term entered separately

variables.name: age_squared
variables.definition: square of centered age
variables.construction: age^2 after centering (whether squared before or after centering is unstated)

variables.name: postsecondary
variables.definition: 1 if the respondent has a post-secondary degree or higher

variables.name: year_dummies
variables.definition: indicator for each survey year, 2001 reference (2002 reference in Model 7; 2005-2008 only in Model 8 with one category omitted)
variables.construction: from GEM_YR
variables.locator: MAIN p.19 Table 1; MAIN p.22 Table 2; S1 p.2 Table A2

variables.name: not_employed
variables.definition: 1 if not currently employed (supplement Model 2 only)
variables.locator: S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 2; MAIN p.10 fn 2

variables.name: suskill
variables.definition: 1 if agrees she or he has the knowledge, skill and experience to start a business (supplement Model 3)
variables.locator: MAIN p.11; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 3

variables.name: fearfail
variables.definition: 1 if fear of failure would prevent starting a business
variables.construction: FEARFAIL = 1 (or 100) -> 1; 0 -> 0
variables.locator: MAIN p.11; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 3

variables.name: knowent
variables.definition: 1 if knows someone personally who started a business in the past two years
variables.locator: MAIN p.11; S1 p.3 Table A3 Model 3

variables.name: plan_b_motivation
variables.definition: 1 if the business owner reports being involved because of 'no better choices for work'; 0 otherwise
variables.construction: OMREASON = 2 -> 1; OMREASON in {1, 3, 4, 6} -> 0 (equivalently OMWHY = -1 -> 1). Treatment of the mixed category (OMREASON = 3) is an open coding decision (spec_space).
variables.locator: MAIN p.14 'Entrepreneurial motivations'; S1 p.2 Table A2 Panel B

variables.name: business_size
variables.definition: log of (number of full-time employees + 1)
variables.construction: ln(OMNOWJOB + 1); GEM does not distinguish full-time from part-time employees (MAIN p.31-32)
variables.locator: MAIN p.14 'Growth orientation'; S1 p.2 Table A2 Panel B note *

variables.name: high_growth_aspirations
variables.definition: 1 if the owner expects to hire more than five additional employees in the next five years
variables.construction: (OMYR5JOB - OMNOWJOB) > 5 -> 1; else 0
variables.coding_of_missing: special codes on either item dropped

variables.name: new_product
variables.definition: 1 if the product/service is new and unfamiliar to all customers

variables.name: new_technology
variables.definition: 1 if the product/service requires technologies less than five years old
variables.construction: Origin: OMNEWT_5 in {1, 2} -> 1; 3 -> 0. Alternative (code 1 only) recorded in spec_space.

variables.name: sole_owner
variables.definition: 1 if the entrepreneur owns all of the business; 0 if ownership is shared
variables.construction: OMOWN = 1 -> 1; OMOWN = 2 -> 0 (alternative: OMOWNERS = 1)

variables.name: business_age
variables.definition: log of years since the founders first received wages, profits or payments in kind; grand-mean centered
variables.construction: years = GEM_YR - first payment year from OMWAGEYR (code scheme varies by survey year; must be decoded); then log. How zero-year businesses are handled is unstated (spec_space).
variables.coding_of_missing: OMWAGEYR 'none yet', don't know, refused, not applicable dropped
variables.locator: MAIN p.15 and fn 15; S1 p.2 Table A2 Panel B note *

variables.name: paid_leave
variables.definition: weeks of full-time-equivalent paid leave available to mothers from the state, computed as wage replacement rate times duration; policy changes lagged one year
variables.construction: Author-built annual database from Ray 2008, Ray et al. 2010, ILO 2012 and OECD Family Database; not available as a ready-made series. Proposed construction: CEPR 2008 FTE weeks for mothers as the 2008 anchor for 21 countries; adjust pre-change years for the eight countries with policy changes using OECD PF2.5 weeks and ILO payment rates; Czech Republic, Iceland and Poland from ILO pages and PF2.5. Apply a one-year lag to changes.
variables.transformations: standardized (z-score across survey-years); squared term also entered
variables.locator: MAIN p.11-12 text and fn 6, 7, 8; S1 p.1 Table A1 note *

variables.name: paid_leave_squared
variables.definition: square of the paid-leave measure
variables.construction: Unstated whether the square of the standardized variable or the standardized square; origin: square of the standardized variable.

variables.name: childcare_spending
variables.definition: public expenditure on childcare services (cash, in-kind, tax) for children under five, as percent of GDP
variables.construction: OECD Family Database (2012 edition) values published for 2005 and 2007; other years imputed by the author (method unstated). Registered current PF3.1 series covers childcare plus pre-primary for all years.
variables.coding_of_missing: imputed by author for missing years
variables.locator: MAIN p.12 text and fn 9; S1 p.1 Table A1 note †

variables.name: women_part_time
variables.definition: percent of women in paid employment who work part time
variables.construction: OECD Labour Force Statistics incidence of part-time employment, women; origin: OECD common definition (under 30 usual weekly hours), share of women's employment. Supplement note says 'female employees'.
variables.locator: MAIN p.12; S1 p.1 Table A1 note ‡

variables.name: gdp_index
variables.definition: UNDP Human Development Report GDP index (log GDP per capita PPP scaled 0-1)
variables.construction: Read from HDR statistical annex tables; mapping of report edition to survey year unstated (reports refer to about two years earlier).
variables.locator: MAIN p.13 ('GDP per capita'); S1 p.1 Table A1 column 'GDP index'

variables.name: unemployment_rate
variables.definition: harmonised unemployment rate, percent of labour force
variables.construction: OECD Main Economic Indicators annual harmonised unemployment rate, total, by country-year
variables.coding_of_missing: Switzerland absent in the registered series; Iceland 2001-2002 absent

variables.name: employment_protection
variables.definition: OECD employment protection index capturing protection of regular and temporary employees from dismissal
variables.construction: Overall EPL index; registered file has no overall series, so construct as the unweighted average of EPL_R and EPL_T (version 1) by country-year. Iceland available only from 2008.

variables.name: social_status
variables.definition: survey-level mean agreement that successful new-business founders have high status and respect
variables.construction: Mean of NBSTATUS = 1 (or 100) among respondents with substantive answers, by country-year (weighted or unweighted unstated). Item has no responses in 2001-2002 in the registered files.

variables.name: women_managers
variables.definition: percent of legislators, senior officials and managers who are women
variables.construction: UNDP HDR gender empowerment measure table; edition-to-year mapping unstated
variables.coding_of_missing: HDR 2010 does not print this indicator

variables.name: fertility_rate
variables.definition: total fertility rate
variables.construction: OECD Family Database SF2.1 by country-year

variables.name: female_x_institution
variables.definition: cross-level interactions of female with paid_leave, paid_leave_squared, childcare_spending and women_part_time
variables.construction: product terms
variables.locator: MAIN p.15; MAIN p.19 Table 1 Model 3; MAIN p.22 Table 2

variables.name: country_id
variables.definition: level-3 grouping
variables.construction: COUNTRY or CTRYALP

variables.name: survey_id
variables.definition: level-2 grouping: country-year survey
variables.construction: COUNTRY x GEM_YR

variables.name: weight
variables.definition: no weighting is mentioned in the article
variables.construction: none (origin unweighted); WEIGHT_L is the registered alternative
